the case), so that the API and the MCP tools answer the same 400.

CategorizationRule.description:
An operation: what recognises transactions (counterparty, label, amount and
its sign), the qualification it copies onto each of them, and an optional
recurrence (period, anchor, expected amount) — spec « Opération et
transaction ».

With a recurrence it is a series the owner expects to see again — rent on
the 5th, Netflix on the 12th: its occurrences are computed by
`RecurrenceSchedule`, never written down, and the transactions that settle
them are attached to it. Without one it is what a categorization rule was:
the first active one by priority files the lines no series claimed.

The class keeps its historical name, its table and its IRI
`/api/recurring_operations/{id}` — the one every view links to, and the one
the live updates name — while the clients read them (MAG-478):
`/api/operations` lists them all, `/api/recurring_operations` the series and
`/api/categorization_rules` the others, with the fields each view knew.

label.description: What the owner calls it; a series has one, an operation without recurrence may.

counterpartyName.description: The payee of an expense, the payer of an income: who the bank names.

counterpartyKey.description: Derived from the name, like a transaction's, so the two compare.

labelPattern.description: Read in the label when there is no counterparty to compare; with neither, the amount and its sign recognise the operation.

direction.description:
The sign an operation without recurrence expects; a series reads it off
its reference amount.

minAmountCents.description:
Absolute amount bounds in cents, for an operation without recurrence: a
debit of 15,99 € matches 1000..2000. A series is bounded by its
reference amount and its tolerance instead.

priority.description:
Among the operations without recurrence, the higher priority files the
line; ties are broken by creation order. A series never competes: it
attaches its own lines first.

isActive.description: A paused operation recognises nothing; a series is never paused, it ends (`endsOn`).

category.description: The default category, inherited by the transactions attached to it.

account.description: A series' account: its currency is the series'. An operation without recurrence reads every account.

period.description: Null for an operation without recurrence: what tells the two apart.

anchorOn.description: Where the series is counted from, never from the previous occurrence.

referenceAmountCents.description: Signed cents: negative is an expense, positive an income.

endsOn.description: The last day an occurrence may fall on; null while the series runs.

applyToExisting.description: Asked on save, never stored: give the existing history to this operation too.

monthlyCostCents.description: What the series costs (negative) or brings in (positive) a month, in cents; null without recurrence.

yearlyCostCents.description: What the series costs (negative) or brings in (positive) a year, in cents; null without recurrence.

ContactCounterparty.description:
One way a contact shows on the owner's statements: « VIR. DE TOM MARTIN »,
« PAYPAL *TOMMARTIN ». Every transfer it recognises is attached to the
contact (`Transaction.contact`); a label belongs to one contact only.

Linked and removed, never edited: a different label is another counterparty.
Read from Doctrine, with the number of transfers it recognises and the date
of the last one, which a search index would hold stale.

« PAYPAL *TOMMARTIN ». Every transfer it recognises is attached to the
contact (`Transaction.contact`); a label belongs to one contact only.

Linked and removed, never edited: a different label is another counterparty.
Read from Doctrine, with the number of transfers it recognises and the date
of the last one, which a search index would hold stale.

Errand.description:
A finished errand: what was bought, where and when (MAG-488). One per store —
ending the errand without naming a store archives one per store the checked
lines were in. Read-only: it is written by EndErrandHandler alone, and read by
the « Courses passées » views, the `list_past_errands` MCP tool and, later,
the « tu en prends souvent » suggestions.

The store's name and each line's label are copied, not referenced only: a
past errand must still read « Lidl · Tomates » once the store or the product
is gone.

store.description: Sets the store and copies its name.

storeName.description: The store's name when the errand ended; null for lines with no store.

Operation.description:
An operation: what recognises transactions (counterparty, label, amount and
its sign), the qualification it copies onto each of them, and an optional
recurrence (period, anchor, expected amount) — spec « Opération et
transaction ».

With a recurrence it is a series the owner expects to see again — rent on
the 5th, Netflix on the 12th: its occurrences are computed by
`RecurrenceSchedule`, never written down, and the transactions that settle
them are attached to it. Without one it is what a categorization rule was:
the first active one by priority files the lines no series claimed.

The class keeps its historical name, its table and its IRI
`/api/recurring_operations/{id}` — the one every view links to, and the one
the live updates name — while the clients read them (MAG-478):
`/api/operations` lists them all, `/api/recurring_operations` the series and
`/api/categorization_rules` the others, with the fields each view knew.

label.description: What the owner calls it; a series has one, an operation without recurrence may.

counterpartyName.description: The payee of an expense, the payer of an income: who the bank names.

counterpartyKey.description: Derived from the name, like a transaction's, so the two compare.

labelPattern.description: Read in the label when there is no counterparty to compare; with neither, the amount and its sign recognise the operation.

direction.description:
The sign an operation without recurrence expects; a series reads it off
its reference amount.

minAmountCents.description:
Absolute amount bounds in cents, for an operation without recurrence: a
debit of 15,99 € matches 1000..2000. A series is bounded by its
reference amount and its tolerance instead.

priority.description:
Among the operations without recurrence, the higher priority files the
line; ties are broken by creation order. A series never competes: it
attaches its own lines first.

isActive.description: A paused operation recognises nothing; a series is never paused, it ends (`endsOn`).

category.description: The default category, inherited by the transactions attached to it.

account.description: A series' account: its currency is the series'. An operation without recurrence reads every account.

period.description: Null for an operation without recurrence: what tells the two apart.

anchorOn.description: Where the series is counted from, never from the previous occurrence.

referenceAmountCents.description: Signed cents: negative is an expense, positive an income.

endsOn.description: The last day an occurrence may fall on; null while the series runs.

applyToExisting.description: Asked on save, never stored: give the existing history to this operation too.

monthlyCostCents.description: What the series costs (negative) or brings in (positive) a month, in cents; null without recurrence.

yearlyCostCents.description: What the series costs (negative) or brings in (positive) a year, in cents; null without recurrence.

PeerDebt.description:
Money between the owner and their contacts (MAG-451): a créance when they
owe the owner — what is left of a shared spend once the owner's part is set —,
a dette the other way round (MAG-452). Split into one share per person.

Read only over REST: it is written through the transaction it comes from
(`PUT /api/finance/transactions/{id}/my-share`). Served from Doctrine, like
the counterparties: what is left to give back moves with every repayment,
a search document would hold it stale. Indexed for the search all the same.

object.description: What it was for: « Gîte Bretagne ». The spend's label by default.

amountCents.description: What the shares add up to.

RecurringOperation.description:
An operation: what recognises transactions (counterparty, label, amount and
its sign), the qualification it copies onto each of them, and an optional
recurrence (period, anchor, expected amount) — spec « Opération et
transaction ».

With a recurrence it is a series the owner expects to see again — rent on
the 5th, Netflix on the 12th: its occurrences are computed by
`RecurrenceSchedule`, never written down, and the transactions that settle
them are attached to it. Without one it is what a categorization rule was:
the first active one by priority files the lines no series claimed.

The class keeps its historical name, its table and its IRI
`/api/recurring_operations/{id}` — the one every view links to, and the one
the live updates name — while the clients read them (MAG-478):
`/api/operations` lists them all, `/api/recurring_operations` the series and
`/api/categorization_rules` the others, with the fields each view knew.

label.description: What the owner calls it; a series has one, an operation without recurrence may.

counterpartyName.description: The payee of an expense, the payer of an income: who the bank names.

counterpartyKey.description: Derived from the name, like a transaction's, so the two compare.

labelPattern.description: Read in the label when there is no counterparty to compare; with neither, the amount and its sign recognise the operation.

direction.description:
The sign an operation without recurrence expects; a series reads it off
its reference amount.

minAmountCents.description:
Absolute amount bounds in cents, for an operation without recurrence: a
debit of 15,99 € matches 1000..2000. A series is bounded by its
reference amount and its tolerance instead.

priority.description:
Among the operations without recurrence, the higher priority files the
line; ties are broken by creation order. A series never competes: it
attaches its own lines first.

isActive.description: A paused operation recognises nothing; a series is never paused, it ends (`endsOn`).

category.description: The default category, inherited by the transactions attached to it.

account.description: A series' account: its currency is the series'. An operation without recurrence reads every account.

period.description: Null for an operation without recurrence: what tells the two apart.

anchorOn.description: Where the series is counted from, never from the previous occurrence.

referenceAmountCents.description: Signed cents: negative is an expense, positive an income.

endsOn.description: The last day an occurrence may fall on; null while the series runs.

applyToExisting.description: Asked on save, never stored: give the existing history to this operation too.

monthlyCostCents.description: What the series costs (negative) or brings in (positive) a month, in cents; null without recurrence.

yearlyCostCents.description: What the series costs (negative) or brings in (positive) a year, in cents; null without recurrence.

tags.name: Contact
tags.description:
A person the owner lends to or borrows from (MAG-450) — one list for both
sides. Their transfers are recognised by the labels in `ContactCounterparty`.

tags.name: ContactCounterparty
tags.description:
One way a contact shows on the owner's statements: « VIR. DE TOM MARTIN »,
« PAYPAL *TOMMARTIN ». Every transfer it recognises is attached to the
contact (`Transaction.contact`); a label belongs to one contact only.

Linked and removed, never edited: a different label is another counterparty.
Read from Doctrine, with the number of transfers it recognises and the date
of the last one, which a search index would hold stale.

tags.name: Loan
tags.description:
A loan being repaid. Its end date is never stored: it falls out of the
capital, the payment and the rate, and a fourth field would contradict
them at the first early repayment.

tags.name: PeerDebt
tags.description:
Money between the owner and their contacts (MAG-451): a créance when they
owe the owner — what is left of a shared spend once the owner's part is set —,
a dette the other way round (MAG-452). Split into one share per person.

Read only over REST: it is written through the transaction it comes from
(`PUT /api/finance/transactions/{id}/my-share`). Served from Doctrine, like
the counterparties: what is left to give back moves with every repayment,
a search document would hold it stale. Indexed for the search all the same.

tags.name: RecurringOperation
tags.description:
An operation: what recognises transactions (counterparty, label, amount and
its sign), the qualification it copies onto each of them, and an optional
recurrence (period, anchor, expected amount) — spec « Opération et
transaction ».

With a recurrence it is a series the owner expects to see again — rent on
the 5th, Netflix on the 12th: its occurrences are computed by
`RecurrenceSchedule`, never written down, and the transactions that settle
them are attached to it. Without one it is what a categorization rule was:
the first active one by priority files the lines no series claimed.

The class keeps its historical name, its table and its IRI
`/api/recurring_operations/{id}` — the one every view links to, and the one
the live updates name — while the clients read them (MAG-478):
`/api/operations` lists them all, `/api/recurring_operations` the series and
`/api/categorization_rules` the others, with the fields each view knew.

tags.name: SafetyCushion
tags.description:
The safety net, configured once per user. Its current amount is never
stored here — it is the balance of the accounts flagged as cushion.

tags.name: Aisle
tags.description:
A shelf of one store, where its products are picked up, in the order the
owner walks through the shop (MAG-493). The same product may be in a
different aisle in each store: {@see ProductAisle}.

The name is checked by the use cases (not blank, unique per store whatever
the case), so that the API and the MCP tools answer the same 400.

tags.name: Errand
tags.description:
A finished errand: what was bought, where and when (MAG-488). One per store —
ending the errand without naming a store archives one per store the checked
lines were in. Read-only: it is written by EndErrandHandler alone, and read by
the « Courses passées » views, the `list_past_errands` MCP tool and, later,
the « tu en prends souvent » suggestions.

The store's name and each line's label are copied, not referenced only: a
past errand must still read « Lidl · Tomates » once the store or the product
is gone.
